title: Dynamical development of long-range spatial coherence in non-equilibrium bosonic condensation
authors: Bianca Rae Fabricante, Dąbrówka Biegańska, Paolo Comaron, Mateusz Król, Matthias Wurdack, Maciej Pieczarka, Mark Steger, David W. Snoke, Kenneth West, Daniele Sanvitto, Dario Ballarini, Dimitrios Trypogeorgos, Loren N. Pfeiffer, Andrew G. Truscott, Marzena Szymańska, Elena A. Ostrovskaya, Eliezer Estrecho
abstract: Development of spontaneous coherence is one of the hallmarks of bosonic condensation in a variety of physical systems, such as cold atoms, confined photons, and hybrid light-matter quasiparticles like exciton polaritons in semiconductors. While spatial coherence is well understood once a steady-state condensate has been established, its temporal evolution as the condensate forms is largely unexplored. Here, we explore the dynamical formation of a non-equilibrium, driven-dissipative exciton-polariton condensate through both time-resolved experiments and numerical modeling. Our study reveals that the spatial coherence is established through two distinct stages. The early-time stage is interaction-driven and features transient oscillations in spatial coherence. This stage is followed by a steady-state regime characterized by a spatially-uniform high degree of coherence that extends over the entire size of the system and persists over time. These stages of spatial coherence development occur in both free flowing and confined exciton-polariton systems that undergo a quench - rapid growth of the condensate starting from two different initial settings. Our study offers a deep insight into the process by which long-range spatial coherence is established in a non-equilibrium bosonic condensate.
summary: This paper investigates how long-range spatial coherence emerges in exciton-polariton condensates that are driven far from equilibrium. Using time-resolved experiments and simulations, the authors demonstrate that coherence develops in two distinct phases: an initial, oscillatory interaction-driven phase, followed by a stable, high-coherence steady state. This sheds light on the complex, non-equilibrium physics governing bosonic condensation.
main_problem: The study investigates the dynamical development of long-range spatial coherence in non-equilibrium bosonic condensation, focusing on the temporal evolution of coherence as the condensate forms.
main_result: Spatial coherence develops through two distinct stages: an early-time, interaction-driven stage featuring transient oscillations, followed by a persistent, spatially-uniform steady-state regime.
method: The research combines time-resolved experiments (using pulsed and continuous wave laser excitation) with numerical modeling to track coherence dynamics.
model_or_system: The system is an exciton-polariton condensate formed in a microcavity, which is a driven-dissipative, non-equilibrium bosonic system.
key_observables: Spatial coherence (measured via the first-order correlation function, g^(1)), condensate density, and coherence length (l_coh).
important_parameters: Detuning ($\Delta$), excitation power relative to the threshold ($P/P_{th}$), and the excitation configuration (Ring-Shaped Pulsed Laser vs. Gaussian Continuous Wave).
main_assumptions: The early-time dynamics are attributed to underlying microscopic processes of energy relaxation and interactions, distinct from simple density oscillations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental setups (RPL and GCW), time-resolved measurements of g^(1) and density, and how coherence length evolves across different detunings and pumping powers.
paper_structure: The paper systematically explores the coherence dynamics using multiple experimental setups (RPL, GCW) and varying physical parameters (detuning, pump power), confirming the two-stage coherence development across different regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides deep insight into the non-equilibrium dynamics of coherence formation in cavity QED systems, offering a detailed picture of how coherence builds up beyond simple steady-state assumptions.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. Two experimental configurations. a) In the ring-shaped pulsed laser (RPL) pump configuration, a pump pulse creates the dynamical polariton condensate trapped inside a ring- shaped excitonic reservoir generated by the pump. The con- densate forms after the arrival of the pulse and subsequently decays, as shown in (b). c) In the Gaussian continuous wave pump (GCW) configuration, a steady-state condensate flow- ing away from the excitation spot is formed. A red-detuned laser pulse is then used to break the condensate. The pulse ini- tiates a rapid polariton density depletion followed by a rapid growth and recovery of the condensate, as shown in (d).

Fig. 2. Typical time evolution of the condensate density and g(1) for (a,b) RPL and (c,d) GCW configurations, with the ra- tios of the pump power relative to the condensation threshold P/Pth = 26 and Bp/Bp,0 = 12, respectively. a) Condensate density evolution (quantified by PL intensity heatmap) and its value integrated over the spatial (x) dimension and normal- ized by the peak value (blue line). b) Condensate coherence heatmap (shown for half of the spatial range, x > 0) and g(1)

Fig. 3. Time-resolved condensate PL and g(1) heatmaps for the excitonic fraction |X|2 = 0.50 and the pump power ratio P/Pth of (a,f) 4, (b,g) 6, (c,h) 17, (d,i) 22, and (e,j) 26 in the TCO regime of the RPL experiment. The blue line is the condensate density quantified by integrating the PL intensity over the spatial (x) dimension and normalizing it by the peak value. The orange line is the spatial coherence integrated over the spatial coordinate (x) and normalized to its peak value.

Fig. 4. Time-resolved condensate PL and g(1) heatmaps for the breaking pulse power ratio Bp/Bp,0 of (a,e) 1, (b,f) 2, (c,g) 4, and (d,h) 8 in the TCO regime of the GCW experiment, after the condensate-breaking pulse. Bp,0 is the threshold pulse power for breaking the condensate. The blue line is the total detected PL intensity at each time normalized to its peak value. The orange line is the spatial coherence integrated along the vertical axis normalized to its peak value.

Fig. 5. Dependence of spatial coherence dynamics on the ex- citonic fraction in the RPL configuration. (a-d) Time-resolved g(1) profile heatmaps at increasing (from a to d) excitonic frac- tion with a fixed pump power (P/Pth ≈26).
